quick: Prophylaxis 2500-3500 IU SC once daily; treatment 115 IU/kg SC once daily
Use if clearly needed; preferred LMWH option in some settings
Caution; minimal oral bioavailability in infant
Caution in severe impairment; consider reduced dose/monitoring
Platelets (HIT), renal function, signs of bleeding; anti-Xa if needed
summary: Bemiparin is a second-generation low molecular weight heparin given subcutaneously once daily for prophylaxis and treatment of venous thromboembolism and for prevention of clotting in extracorporeal circuits. It acts mainly via antithrombin-mediated inhibition of factor Xa. It is not FDA-approved; information is based on EMA/SmPC and BNF sources. Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and bleeding are key risks.
indications: Prevention of venous thromboembolism in surgical (orthopedic and general) and high-risk medical patients
Treatment of established deep vein thrombosis with or without pulmonary embolism
Prevention of clotting in the extracorporeal circuit during hemodialysis
Extended prophylaxis after major orthopedic surgery (per SmPC)

dosage.n: First dose 2 h before or 6 h after surgery
Continue 7-10 days or until ambulant; extended to ~28-35 days for hip
Typically 5-9 days, overlap with oral anticoagulant

dosage.d: Single bolus into arterial line: ~2500 IU (<60 kg) or 3500 IU (>=60 kg)

admin: Administer by deep subcutaneous injection, usually into the anterolateral or posterolateral abdominal wall
Alternate injection sites; do not rub the site after injection
Do not expel the air bubble from prefilled syringes before injecting
Do not administer by intramuscular route
For hemodialysis, inject as a single bolus into the arterial line at the start of the session
moa: Bemiparin potentiates antithrombin III, producing strong inhibition of activated factor Xa with relatively little inhibition of thrombin (factor IIa), reflecting its low molecular weight and high anti-Xa/anti-IIa ratio. This blocks propagation of the coagulation cascade and thrombus formation while having a relatively predictable, weight-based anticoagulant effect.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to bemiparin, heparin or pork products
Active major bleeding or high-risk bleeding lesion (e.g., active peptic ulcer)
relative: Recent CNS, ophthalmic or otic surgery
Concurrent neuraxial anesthesia/spinal puncture (epidural hematoma risk)

preg: Heparins do not cross the placenta; bemiparin may be used during pregnancy when anticoagulation is needed and benefit justifies use. Avoid neuraxial anesthesia within recommended intervals. Use product without benzyl alcohol where possible.
lact: Limited data; any excreted drug is poorly absorbed orally by the infant. Use with caution if breastfeeding, weighing benefit and risk.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment; LMWH accumulates as renal function declines. Consider dose reduction and anti-Xa monitoring in severe impairment (e.g., CrCl <30 mL/min).
hepatic: Use with caution in severe hepatic impairment because of increased bleeding risk and altered coagulation.

major: Other anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs, heparin) - additive bleeding (except planned overlap)
Antiplatelet agents (aspirin, clopidogrel, NSAIDs at antiplatelet doses) - increased bleeding
moderate: Drugs raising serum potassium (heparins can cause hyperkalemia) - additive hyperkalemia with ACE inhibitors/ARBs/potassium-sparing diuretics
interactions.alcohol: Limit; heavy use increases bleeding and fall risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Prolongs anti-Xa activity; APTT is relatively unaffected; may cause mild hyperkalemia and transaminase elevation.

emergency: Spinal/epidural hematoma (back pain, leg weakness, bladder/bowel dysfunction)

monitoring: Platelet count at baseline and periodically to detect heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
Renal function, especially with prolonged use or impairment
Serum potassium in at-risk patients; anti-factor Xa levels when monitoring is indicated (renal impairment, obesity, pregnancy)
counsel: Inject under the skin of the abdomen as shown; rotate sites and do not rub afterward
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, black stools or blood in urine
Seek urgent care for back pain with leg numbness/weakness if you have had a spinal procedure
Tell all providers you are on a blood thinner before any surgery or dental work
Avoid aspirin/NSAIDs unless approved by your doctor
pk: Anti-Xa effect within 2-3 hours of subcutaneous injection
Maximum anti-Xa activity approximately 2-4 hours after dosing
Store below 25-30 C; do not freeze
pearls: NOTE: Not FDA-approved; information based on EMA/SmPC and BNF, not a US FDA label
Second-generation LMWH with the longest half-life and highest anti-Xa/anti-IIa ratio, enabling once-daily dosing
Protamine sulfate only partially reverses LMWH activity (roughly 60% of anti-Xa)
Check platelets to detect HIT; avoid in patients with prior immune HIT
Respect timing intervals around neuraxial (spinal/epidural) anesthesia to avoid hematoma
missed: If a once-daily dose is missed, give it as soon as remembered on the same day; if it is close to the next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not give two doses together.
overdose: Overdose may cause hemorrhage. Discontinue bemiparin and apply supportive measures; protamine sulfate partially neutralizes anti-Xa activity (approximately 1 mg protamine per 100 anti-Xa IU). Repeat protamine may be needed because of bemiparin's longer half-life.
